label: Strict past, inclusive past and modal seriality
term: strict past, inclusive past and modal seriality
resolution: Strict accessibility s<t on times through now requires an earlier time for seriality; with the supplied Preorder this is exactly existing PastIsInfinite(<)now. Inclusive accessibility s≤t permits self-witnesses and is serial even at an earliest time. Therefore D validity on strict past encodes no first past moment instead of proving it, whereas inclusive T/D do not imply beginninglessness. PastIsFinite means an earlier-free time through now, not finite duration or finite event cardinality. These frames interpret abstract indices as times; Ontic worlds/complete histories and time points remain distinct, and no causal arrows cross alternative worlds.
